series_label: 河西走廊历史阅读 · 连载 20
title_en: At the Receiving Desk: Opening a Han Frontier Letter
title_zh: 文书抵达以后：汉代边塞官署怎样收文启封
lead: 邮书沿河西驿路送达后，收件官署怎样确认它来自何处、何时抵达？

paragraphs.en: A letter could reach a frontier office and still leave a difficult question: who was authorized to open it? Yesterday's story followed the records that allowed a late or damaged letter to be traced backward along the Hexi road. Arrival created a different responsibility. The receiving office had to identify the sender, record the arrival, and inspect the sealed packet before its contents could become official business. Wooden documents from the northwestern Han frontier preserve parts of that work. They do not give us a complete day in one office, but they show why delivery was a beginning rather than an end.
paragraphs.zh: 一封文书送到边塞官署，仍会留下一个难题：谁有权启封？昨天的文章讲述了怎样依据记录，沿河西驿路倒查迟误或受损的邮书。抵达又带来另一种责任：收文官署必须辨认发件者、记录到达，并检查封缄的文书，才能将其中内容纳入公务。汉代西北边塞的木简保存了部分工作痕迹。它们没有完整记录某间官署的一天，却说明送达只是起点。

paragraphs.en: A packet was more than writing hidden under a cover. An official seal impressed into clay could identify the authority behind it. A 2024 study of Han seal records notes that transmission entries could shorten a seal's name when local workers could still recognize it. Receiving records followed a stricter practice: examples copied the seal inscription as it appeared. This mattered because an office could receive letters from places beyond its own district. A familiar local abbreviation might make sense on the road but create uncertainty at the destination. The receiver needed a record that another reader could check later.
paragraphs.zh: 文书包裹不只是封套下的文字。钤在封泥上的官印能够标明其背后的权力机关。一项2024年的汉代印文研究指出，传行记录有时简写印文，只要本地经手者仍能认出；收文记录则更严格，所举实例按原样抄录印文。原因在于官署可能收到辖区以外的来文。路上通用的本地简称，到达终点后或许难以辨识。收文者需要留下日后他人也能核查的记录。

paragraphs.en: One slip from Xuanquan gives this distinction a concrete form. Its front carries an official communication associated with Xiaogu county near Dunhuang. The back records the Xiaogu magistrate's seal and a day of arrival. The study treats that back text as an arrival record, rather than a new message. These short marks answer questions the letter's main text cannot answer by itself: which sealed document was received, and when? The slip does not prove that every station used precisely the same layout. It does show that the reverse of a document could become a place for administrative evidence.
paragraphs.zh: 一枚悬泉简让这种区别变得具体。正面是一份与敦煌附近效谷县有关的官文；背面记下效谷长印和到达的日期。那项研究将背文视为收文记录，而不是另一封新信。这些简短记号回答了正文自身无法回答的问题：收到的是哪份封缄文书，又是在何时？这枚简不能证明每个站点都采用完全相同的布局，却表明文书背面也能成为行政证据的载体。

paragraphs.en: The next question was opening. A separate study of Qin and Han opening records, based on excavated slips, examines the northwestern military system, including the Juyan frontier. Its author argues that clerks and military officers could open and read documents under the authority of a senior official, rather than simply passing all letters into a separate set of departments. That is an interpretation of surviving forms, not a rule we can impose on every Hexi county office. The study also proposes a sequence: mark the incoming seal and date, copy the information into a register, and add a formal opening signature. Because the sequence is reconstructed, its individual steps should not be mistaken for a surviving account of one complete packet.
paragraphs.zh: 接下来是启封问题。另一项依据出土简牍研究秦汉启封记录的论文，考察了居延边塞在内的西北军事系统。作者认为，书吏和军吏可在高级官员的权力名义下开启、阅读文书，而非一律先由不同部门分流。这是对存世格式的解释，不能直接套到每个河西县署。论文还推测一种次序：先在封检上记收文印章与日期，再誊入簿籍，最后由开启者作形式上的签署。由于这一流程是重建，不能将各步骤误当作某一封文书的完整实录。

paragraphs.en: The two studies meet at a practical point. A seal inscription was useful only if someone could compare it with the document and the receiving record. The seal study says faithful copying at opening could help detect a mismatch between the stated sender and the text inside. It also gives a case in which the title of the official who issued a letter differs from the seal used to close it. The receiving record preserves the seal actually seen. A difference did not automatically mean fraud: an officer might use a superior's seal. But recording the difference kept the question visible instead of silently correcting the evidence.
paragraphs.zh: 两项研究在一个实际问题上相交：只有能够将印文、正文和收文记录互相比对，抄录印文才有用。印文研究指出，启封时如实抄录，有助于发现发件者题名与内文不合的情况。论文还举出一例：发文官的职称与封缄所用印章并不相同，而收文记录保留了实际看到的印文。差异并不自动等于造假，官吏可能使用上级印章；但记下差异，便不会悄悄改写证据。

paragraphs.en: There were people behind these small marks. A courier's work ended with a handover, while a clerk now had to make the packet legible to an office. Writing the date or copying the seal placed that clerk within a chain of responsibility. A mistaken character could make the origin harder to establish later; a missing arrival date could weaken a check on timing. These are practical implications of the records, not documented mistakes by a named worker. The surviving slips seldom tell us how long the clerk waited, whether the office was crowded, or what pressure an order created. Their silence should keep the scene modest.
paragraphs.zh: 这些细小记号背后有人。送信人的任务随交接告一段落，书吏则须让整间官署能够辨识文书。写下日期或抄录印文，也把书吏置于责任链中。一个错字可能使后来更难确认来源；缺失到达日期也可能削弱时限核查。这些是记录的实际含义，并非某位具名工作人员犯错的史实。存世简牍很少告诉我们书吏等了多久、官署是否繁忙，或命令带来什么压力。面对这种沉默，场景只能写得克制。

paragraphs.en: The evidence also limits what we can say about action after opening. An arrival mark proves receipt; an opening notation can identify who formally opened a letter. Neither alone shows that the order was obeyed, copied for another office, or challenged. Those results require other records. The distinction matters on a long frontier road: a government could design a system for delivering and registering instructions without guaranteeing that every instruction was carried out. We can follow the paperwork to the desk, but we cannot turn its arrival into an invented decision.
paragraphs.zh: 证据也限制了我们对启封后行动的判断。到达记号证明收文；启封记载可以指出谁在形式上开启文书。单凭任何一项，都不能证明命令得到执行、转抄到另一官署，或遭到质疑；这些结果需要其他记录。在漫长的边塞道路上，这个区别很重要：官府可以建立传递和登记指令的制度，却不保证每道指令都被落实。我们可以沿文书走到案头，却不能把它的抵达写成一项虚构的决定。

paragraphs.en: So the journey begun at Yuli does not end with a courier crossing a threshold. At a receiving office, seal, date, and opening record changed a traveling object into a document that could be checked and read. The details varied among surviving slips, and scholars still debate how to reconstruct the full workflow. Yet the central answer is firm: receiving a Han letter was recorded work, with identifiable hands and limits of proof. A future installment can follow a particular order only when its text and later response survive together. Until then, the open packet tells us how an office knew what had arrived, not what it ultimately chose to do.
paragraphs.zh: 因此，从鱼离开始追踪的路程，并不会在送信人跨过官署门槛时结束。到了收文官署，印章、日期和启封记录使一件在途实物成为可核查、可阅读的公文。存世简牍的细节并不一致，完整流程的重建仍有讨论余地。但核心答案明确：汉代收文是一项有记录的工作，能够看见经手环节，也必须承认举证边界。后文只有在某道命令的文本及后续回应同时留存时，才能继续追踪其执行。眼前这份启开的文书告诉我们官署如何确认收到什么，却没有告诉我们最终作了什么决定。

questions.q: Why did receiving records copy seal inscriptions carefully?
questions.a: The receiving office needed to identify and later check letters from different places.

questions.q: What does the Xuanquan slip's reverse record?
questions.a: The Xiaogu magistrate's seal and an arrival date.

questions.q: Does an arrival mark prove that an order was obeyed?
questions.a: No. It proves receipt; action requires separate evidence.
